Fresh_Case_11.name: Cross_Border_Payment_Licensing
Fresh_Case_11.original_title: Cross-Border Payments Licensing Across Regulatory Blocs
Fresh_Case_11.background_context: In 2026, a mid-size payments firm operates licensed remittance corridors between the EU, the Gulf, Southeast Asia, and Latin America. Each bloc now enforces distinct licensing, KYC, and settlement-currency rules, and several corridors face new capital-control measures. Margins differ sharply by corridor, and local banking partners have uneven technical maturity.
Fresh_Case_11.business_problem: Design a financial-operations strategy for sustaining and expanding cross-border payment corridors under divergent licensing regimes, balancing compliance cost, settlement risk, and partner economics across regions.

Fresh_Case_12.name: Subscription_Pricing_Localization
Fresh_Case_12.original_title: Subscription Pricing and Payment Localization for a Global Media Service
Fresh_Case_12.background_context: In 2026, a global streaming service is shifting from uniform USD pricing to localized subscription models. Purchasing power, preferred payment rails (mobile money, QR systems, installments), family-sharing norms, and attitudes toward recurring billing differ strongly across its African, South Asian, and Latin American growth markets, while headquarters still reports revenue in consolidated USD.
Fresh_Case_12.business_problem: Propose a pricing and business-model strategy for localizing subscriptions across markets with different income levels, payment habits, and household-sharing norms, while keeping consolidated unit economics defensible to investors.

Fresh_Case_13.name: Microinsurance_Distribution_Models
Fresh_Case_13.background_context: By 2026, an insurer is piloting climate-linked microinsurance for smallholder farmers in East Africa, South Asia, and Central America. Distribution candidates include cooperatives, mobile-network agents, religious community groups, and fintech apps. Trust in formal insurance, expectations of claim speed, and the perceived legitimacy of different intermediaries vary greatly by region, and actuarial data quality is uneven.
Fresh_Case_13.business_problem: Design distribution and business-model options for climate microinsurance across regions with different trust regimes and intermediation norms, addressing acquisition cost, claim credibility, and portfolio risk.

Fresh_Case_14.name: Green_Bond_Financing_Structure
Fresh_Case_14.original_title: Green-Bond Financing for a Multinational Industrial Group
Fresh_Case_14.background_context: In 2026, an industrial group with plants in Europe, North Africa, and Southeast Asia wants to finance decarbonization retrofits through green bonds. Taxonomy definitions, disclosure standards, and investor ESG expectations differ across the EU, Gulf, and Asian capital markets, and internal plants report emissions with inconsistent measurement quality. Rating agencies and regional banks give conflicting guidance.
Fresh_Case_14.business_problem: Propose a financing strategy that structures green-bond issuance across markets with divergent taxonomies and disclosure standards, while managing measurement-quality risk and protecting the group's credibility with investors.

Fresh_Case_15.name: Franchise_Royalty_Restructuring
Fresh_Case_15.original_title: Franchise Royalty Restructuring Under Currency Volatility
Fresh_Case_15.background_context: In 2026, a quick-service restaurant franchisor with thousands of outlets across Turkey, Egypt, Nigeria, Indonesia, and Brazil faces franchisees squeezed by currency depreciation and local inflation. Fixed USD-denominated royalties are becoming unsustainable in several markets, and franchisee associations in different countries are organizing collectively, while company-owned stores in stable-currency markets remain profitable.
Fresh_Case_15.business_problem: Design a royalty and franchise-financing restructuring approach that preserves long-term brand economics across markets with different currency stability, inflation, and collective-bargaining cultures.

Fresh_Case_16.name: Voice_Assistant_Cultural_Adaptation
Fresh_Case_16.original_title: Voice Assistant Product Adaptation for Honorific Languages
Fresh_Case_16.background_context: In 2026, a consumer-electronics maker is adapting its smart-home voice assistant for Japan, Korea, Thailand, and the Gulf. Languages differ in honorific systems, users differ in comfort with commanding a device aloud, household structures vary (multigenerational homes are common), and local privacy expectations about always-listening devices diverge from the product's Western design assumptions.
Fresh_Case_16.business_problem: Propose a product-adaptation strategy for a voice assistant entering honorific-language markets, covering interaction style, household roles, privacy signaling, and feature prioritization.

Fresh_Case_17.name: EdTech_Platform_Curriculum_Fit
Fresh_Case_17.original_title: EdTech Platform Localization Against National Curricula
Fresh_Case_17.background_context: In 2026, an adaptive-learning startup is expanding from the US into Vietnam, Saudi Arabia, France, and Kenya. Each country mandates different curricula, language-of-instruction rules, and attitudes toward foreign educational content; parents and teachers hold different beliefs about screen time and standardized testing; and government procurement processes differ from direct-to-consumer purchasing.
Fresh_Case_17.business_problem: Design a product strategy for localizing an adaptive-learning platform across countries with mandated curricula, different parental attitudes, and mixed procurement channels, balancing a shared technology core against local fit.

Fresh_Case_18.name: Wearable_Health_Regulatory_Pathways
Fresh_Case_18.original_title: Wearable Health-Feature Rollout Under Divergent Medical Regulations
Fresh_Case_18.background_context: In 2026, a wearables company has developed sleep-apnea screening features whose regulatory classification differs by market: medical device in the EU and Japan, wellness feature in several emerging markets, and a pending classification in the US. Clinical-validation expectations, physician-endorsement norms, and consumers' trust in health claims vary regionally, and the feature pipeline includes five further health capabilities.
Fresh_Case_18.business_problem: Propose a product and regulatory-rollout strategy for health features with divergent classifications across markets, sequencing launches, validation investments, and credibility-building with clinicians and consumers.

Fresh_Case_19.name: Agri_Sensor_Platform_Emerging_Markets
Fresh_Case_19.original_title: Agricultural Sensor Platform for Fragmented Smallholder Markets
Fresh_Case_19.background_context: In 2026, an agri-tech company that sells precision-farming sensor bundles to large farms in North America and Europe is entering India, Kenya, and Vietnam, where farms are small, fragmented, and often reached only through cooperatives or input dealers. Connectivity, hardware affordability, literacy demands, and the value farmers place on different data outputs differ fundamentally from the company's existing markets.
Fresh_Case_19.business_problem: Design a product strategy for adapting a precision-agriculture platform to smallholder markets, covering hardware simplification, delivery partnerships, and which analytics features to prioritize or drop.

Fresh_Case_20.name: Gaming_Monetization_Cultural_Norms
Fresh_Case_20.original_title: Game Monetization Design Across Regulatory and Cultural Norms
Fresh_Case_20.background_context: In 2026, a mobile-game publisher operates one global title with regional monetization variants. Loot-box restrictions now bind in Belgium and the Netherlands, probability disclosure is mandatory in Korea and China, and cultural attitudes toward pay-to-win mechanics, gift-giving events, and cosmetic spending differ across Japan, the Gulf, Brazil, and the US. Player-protection advocacy groups coordinate across borders.
Fresh_Case_20.business_problem: Propose a monetization and product-governance strategy that keeps one global game profitable under divergent loot-box regulations and culturally different spending norms, without fragmenting the player experience irreparably.

Fresh_Case_21.name: ASEAN_Manufacturing_Footprint
Fresh_Case_21.original_title: ASEAN Manufacturing Footprint After Tariff Realignments
Fresh_Case_21.background_context: In 2026, an industrial-equipment maker that historically manufactured in one East Asian hub is evaluating a multi-country ASEAN footprint after tariff realignments and new rules-of-origin requirements. Candidate countries differ in labor skill, supplier depth, logistics quality, incentive regimes, and political stability, while the firm's engineering teams resist splitting production across sites.
Fresh_Case_21.business_problem: Develop a market-entry and footprint strategy for relocating manufacturing capacity across ASEAN candidates, weighing tariff exposure, supplier ecosystems, and organizational feasibility.

Fresh_Case_22.name: GCC_Retail_Joint_Venture
Fresh_Case_22.original_title: Retail Expansion into the Gulf via Joint Venture
Fresh_Case_22.background_context: In 2026, a European grocery retailer is entering Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Qatar through joint ventures with local family conglomerates. Ownership rules, localization-of-workforce mandates, Ramadan-driven seasonality, store-format preferences, and the balance of power between foreign operators and local partners differ from the retailer's previous European expansions.
Fresh_Case_22.business_problem: Propose a market-entry strategy for Gulf retail expansion via joint ventures, covering partner selection, governance, format adaptation, and workforce-localization compliance.

Fresh_Case_23.name: African_Bank_Acquisition_Integration
Fresh_Case_23.original_title: Post-Acquisition Integration of Regional Banks Across Africa
Fresh_Case_23.background_context: In 2026, a pan-African banking group has acquired banks in Nigeria, Kenya, and Morocco. Each acquired bank has different core-banking systems, regulatory supervisors, language environments, and entrenched local management cultures. Group strategy calls for unified digital products, but regulators and customers in each country expect local responsiveness and continuity.
Fresh_Case_23.business_problem: Design an integration and market-consolidation strategy for a multi-country banking acquisition, sequencing technology migration, brand decisions, and management alignment under distinct regulators.

Fresh_Case_25.name: LATAM_D2C_Cosmetics_Launch
Fresh_Case_25.original_title: Direct-to-Consumer Cosmetics Launch Across Latin America
Fresh_Case_25.background_context: In 2026, an Asian beauty brand is launching direct-to-consumer in Mexico, Colombia, and Brazil. Beauty norms, shade-range expectations, influencer ecosystems, marketplace dominance versus owned channels, and social-commerce habits differ by country, and legacy multilevel-marketing beauty firms hold deep distribution and consumer trust in each market.
Fresh_Case_25.business_problem: Design a launch and communications strategy for a D2C cosmetics brand entering three Latin American markets with different beauty norms, channel structures, and incumbent distribution models.

Fresh_Case_26.name: Ramadan_Campaign_Global_Brand
Fresh_Case_26.original_title: Seasonal Faith-Based Campaigns for a Global Food Brand
Fresh_Case_26.background_context: In 2026, a global food brand runs seasonal campaigns tied to Ramadan in the Gulf, North Africa, and Southeast Asia, alongside Lunar New Year and Diwali campaigns elsewhere. Past campaigns drew praise in some markets and accusations of shallow or inaccurate cultural representation in others; agencies differ by region, and social-media scrutiny now amplifies both praise and backlash within hours.
Fresh_Case_26.business_problem: Propose a communications framework for faith-based and cultural seasonal campaigns that achieves authenticity across regions, defines approval safeguards, and manages cross-border scrutiny.

Fresh_Case_27.name: KContent_Dubbing_Streaming
Fresh_Case_27.original_title: Korean Content Localization Strategy for a Streaming Platform
Fresh_Case_27.background_context: In 2026, a streaming platform's Korean-content slate is its fastest-growing category across Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Latin America, and Europe. Audiences differ in subtitle-versus-dubbing preferences, tolerance for adaptation edits, and sensitivity to historical and cultural references; dubbing-studio quality and costs vary widely by language, and fandom communities organize transnationally.
Fresh_Case_27.business_problem: Design a localization and marketing strategy for Korean content across regions with different dubbing expectations, cultural sensitivities, and fandom dynamics, allocating a limited localization budget.

Fresh_Case_29.name: Semiconductor_Lab_Materials_DualSourcing
Fresh_Case_29.original_title: Dual-Sourcing Specialty Materials for Semiconductor Manufacturing
Fresh_Case_29.background_context: In 2026, a semiconductor manufacturer depends on specialty gases and photoresists supplied from a small number of countries facing export-control volatility. Qualifying alternative suppliers in other regions takes 12-24 months per material, quality standards are unforgiving, and some suppliers are reluctant to commit capacity without long-term offtake agreements that finance teams resist.
Fresh_Case_29.business_problem: Propose a supply-chain resilience strategy for dual-sourcing critical semiconductor materials, balancing qualification lead times, quality risk, and long-term commitment economics.

Fresh_Case_30.name: Cold_Chain_Vaccine_Distribution
Fresh_Case_30.original_title: Cold-Chain Distribution for Vaccines Across African Regions
Fresh_Case_30.background_context: In 2026, a pharmaceutical logistics firm is contracted to distribute temperature-sensitive vaccines across West and East Africa. Road quality, customs dwell times, electricity reliability, and last-mile arrangements with ministries of health differ sharply by corridor; some routes require passive cooling containers while others justify powered units; and seasonal weather windows constrain delivery schedules.
Fresh_Case_30.business_problem: Design a cold-chain distribution strategy across African corridors with different infrastructure and institutional constraints, covering equipment choices, corridor sequencing, and contingency planning for spoilage risk.

Fresh_Case_31.name: Remote_Team_Compensation_Equity
Fresh_Case_31.original_title: Location-Based Compensation Fairness for Distributed Teams
Fresh_Case_31.background_context: In 2026, a fully remote software company employs people in 30 countries. Its location-adjusted pay bands, introduced earlier, now generate friction: engineers in Warsaw and Lisbon compare salaries with peers in Berlin and Toronto on public forums, new labor-market data complicates band setting, and several countries now require pay-transparency disclosures that expose internal gaps.
Fresh_Case_31.business_problem: Design a compensation-policy approach for a globally distributed workforce that balances cost-of-labor logic, internal fairness perceptions, and new pay-transparency laws across jurisdictions.

Fresh_Case_32.name: Gig_Worker_Representative_Councils
Fresh_Case_32.original_title: Gig-Worker Representation Models Across Labor Regimes
Fresh_Case_32.background_context: In 2026, a global delivery platform faces new gig-worker representation rules: worker councils in parts of the EU, reclassification pressures in some Latin American countries, and self-regulatory codes in Southeast Asia. Rider collectives already organize informally in several cities, and management's engagement norms were designed for a single home market.
Fresh_Case_32.business_problem: Propose a labor-relations strategy for a delivery platform under divergent gig-worker representation regimes, defining engagement structures, bargaining boundaries, and consistency across regions.
